title: Apache Spark: RDDs, DataFrames and Spark SQL

videos.script: Spark is a driver program, a session, and a recipe. {{driver}} You write what you want. Spark writes it down and does nothing. Not one line of a file is read until you ask for an answer. {{lazy}} That recipe is called the lineage, and it is why Spark can lose an executor and carry on. It recomputes the lost pieces from the files. {{lineage}} This lesson asks the same questions three ways. With RDDs, the original API of functions on records. With DataFrames, tables with typed columns. And with plain SQL. {{three}} Along the way, two measurements you will remember. Guessing a schema cost forty seconds. A Python function cost twice the time of the built-in one. {{costs}} By the end, the clicks are rewritten as Parquet, the layer every later lesson reads. {{silver}}
